meta.hypothesis: Decompose the Geant4 289 s single-thread wall-clock (E15b) into fixed overhead (process init + DNA physics-table construction) vs event-loop, to test the apple-to-apple concern that the 455x speedup is inflated by Geant4 init counted against it while WGSL is dispatch-only.
meta.method: Init-probe: identical validation macro with /run/beamOn 16 instead of 4096, timed externally. fixed + 16*p = probe; fixed + 4096*p = full(E15b). Solve for fixed and per-primary p.
meta.passBar: none — measurement. Reports the corrected event-loop-only speedup.
meta.note_self_correction: This REFUTES the earlier L6 doc claim (~160 s serial overhead / ~200x pure-tracking), which came from a 2-point Amdahl estimate on the MT-8 1.62x scaling. That estimate was wrong: measured init is ~2 s, not ~160 s. The MT-8 sublinearity is instead attributable to row-wise ntuple merging (a serialization point seen in the Geant4 stdout) and/or P/E-core heterogeneity, not init.

summary.headline: Geant4 init+table-build = ~2.1 s (0.7% of 289 s); event-loop-only speedup is 452x, statistically identical to the 455x whole-process figure. The init confound is NOT material — the earlier '~200x pure tracking' claim was wrong and is retracted.

cross_check_256primary.note: A separate 256-primary run lands within 0.3 s of the linear model derived from the 16- and 4096-primary points — independently confirms the ~2 s init and 0.070 s/primary decomposition.

ntuple_io_measured.note: MEASURED (2-point, near-perfectly linear: fixed overhead ~0.1 MB). Earlier ~6.8 GB was an extrapolation; now confirmed at 1.65 MB/primary.

residual_asymmetries: Geant4 289 s includes ~6.8 GB of per-event ntuple I/O to dna.root (MEASURED, 1.65 MB/primary; the row-wise merge is the likely cause of the poor MT-8 1.62x scaling); WGSL 635 ms excludes its ~87 MB rad_buf/dose dump write. A no-ntuple Geant4 build (E15-fairer) would isolate how much wall-time this adds — the 256-primary timing matching the model suggests the fast Apple SSD keeps up so it is interleaved rather than a large serial block, but this is not yet isolated. So 452x is a mild over-estimate of a compute-only comparison.
WGSL 635 ms excludes device init + shader compile (~seconds, roughly symmetric with Geant4's ~2 s init).
summary.fusion_contribution_unchanged: Kernel fusion contributes ~2x to the tracking pipeline (Phase A fused 14.4 ms vs ~704 ms naive is 2% of the 635 ms; Phase B is an un-fused wavefront) — independent of this Geant4 measurement, from E16+E15.
